subject: Clarify indemnity scope and evidence requirements for MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Margaret Lee <margaret.lee@skyward.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@skyward.ai
Date: 2025-12-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify indemnity scope for pending MSA

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we can move the MSA/order form through procurement we need a bit more clarity on the indemnity carve for third-party IP claims tied to model output. A few quick questions: 

- Will Redwood accept defense for third-party claims alleging infringement caused by model output generated via the hosted API?
- If yes, what evidence will you require to trigger defense (logs, prompt history, model id, sample outputs)?
- Would Redwood accept a monetary cap or deductible tied to order form spend or insurance limits?

Procurement also asked for an example redline and a realistic timeline for legal review. I attached our security questionnaire for context.

We'd like to keep momentum on the deal (DEAL-78412) — can you get back with proposed language and evidence list this week?

Best,
Margaret
Head of Legal Operations
Skyward Systems
Attachment: skyward-security-questionnaire.pdf

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Margaret Lee <margaret.lee@skyward.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2025-12-10T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify indemnity scope for pending MSA

Margaret —

Appreciate the clear questions. High level answer up front: we can accept indemnity for a narrow set of third-party IP claims that are attributable to the service as delivered by Redwood (service defects, model implementation issues), but we need carveouts for customer-supplied content and prompts. Below are two pragmatic options for quick procurement review: 

Option A (Customer-lean): Redwood agrees to defend and indemnify for third-party claims alleging that Redwood's service as provided infringes a third party's IP, subject to a cap equal to 1x annual committed spend and standard cooperation/notice requirements. Redwood reserves the right to select counsel if the claim implicates core model IP.

Option B (Redwood-lean): Redwood will reimburse reasonable damages finally awarded against Customer for third-party infringement claims attributable solely to the service; Redwood controls settlement rights and has a lower cap tied to a per-claim limit.

Evidence required to trigger either path: request notice within 30 days, sample outputs, request-id and timestamps, relevant prompt text (when available), and a copy of the third-party claim. We typically ask engineering for a short evidence pull (logs + model id + tokenized prompt) — 3–5 business days after notice.

Attached is a redline that maps the above options to MSA language and suggests a mutual definition for 'Model-Generated Output' and 'Customer Content'.

Proposed timeline: legal redline back to you by 2025-12-18, procurement sign-off by 2025-12-22, execution via DocuSign shortly after. If procurement needs an explicit deductible or insurance floor we can surface that in the order form.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through the options.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Director, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachment: MSA_redline_indemnity_20251210.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2025-12-11T08:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify indemnity scope for pending MSA

Team —

Quick legal calibration: I reviewed Margaret's note and Olga's two-option approach. My recommendations to keep risk bounded while remaining competitive: 

- Narrow trigger language to claims alleging that the Service, as provided by Redwood (specific model version + hosted runtime), infringes a third party's patent/copyright. Exclude: (i) Customer-provided prompts, (ii) customer fine-tuned models, (iii) outputs that reproduce customer provided content.
- Require written notice within 30 days of claim, and provide Redwood 45 days to investigate before any settlement that binds Redwood.
- Include cooperation and privilege-preserving evidence transfer (redact where necessary).
- Cap: prefer a cap equal to 1x annual committed spend for hosted subscriptions; for non-committed orders use a per-claim cap equal to 6 months of average monthly spend. Consider adding an insurance-first backstop if procurement pushes.

Evidence list to include in procurement packet (suggested stub for external):
- Claim document (court filing or notice)
- Representative model outputs with timestamps
- Request ids and model id/version
- Prompts and metadata showing whether prompt was customer-supplied
- Engineering reproduction notes (if Redwood asked to reproduce)

I attached a simple evidence_template.xlsx you can share with the customer to speed triage. Ben — confirm the committed spend number we should reference for DEAL-78412 and whether procurement needs a deductible or carrier details.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: evidence_template.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Margaret Lee <margaret.lee@skyward.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-12-14T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify indemnity scope for pending MSA

Margaret —

Thanks for raising this and for the questionnaire. We discussed internally and want to move forward with a defend-and-indemnify compromise that should be acceptable to procurement: Redwood will accept defense for third-party IP claims attributable to the service as delivered (model+runtime) with a cap equal to 1x the annual committed spend for the Order Form on DEAL-78412. We will exclude customer-supplied prompts and customer-provided training data.

Next steps: 
- Olga will send a narrow redline that maps this compromise into the MSA (you have the draft attached).
- If procurement is OK, we aim to get a redline returned by 2025-12-18.
- Target signature by 2025-12-22 and DocuSign execution the same day.

Link to order form draft and procurement page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/deals/pages/DEAL-78412/order-form-draft
DocuSign placeholder: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/abc123-placeholder

Attachment: order_form_draft.pdf

If procurement wants a conversation about insurance-first approaches we'll loop in our insurance broker, but the defend+cap approach should unblock most customers. Happy to get on a call Thursday afternoon if helpful.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
